topics.label: 12. The core data sheet and the core safety information
13. Mapping a local label and recording deviations
15. Implementation: from approval to the pharmacy shelf

questions.q: What is the CCSI?
options: The safety part of the company core data sheet
A US FDA form for safety changes
The local label in the company's home country
A list of adverse events from one clinical study
questions.why: The Company Core Safety Information is the safety subset of the CCDS that the company wants in every local label.

questions.q: In a periodic benefit-risk report, a reaction that is in the CCSI is called…
questions.why: ICH E2C(R2) uses the CCSI as the reference safety information: reactions in it are listed, others unlisted.

questions.q: Which part of the CCDS may most legitimately differ between markets?
questions.why: Indications depend on what each agency approved. Core safety statements should be in every label unless a deviation is justified.

questions.q: What usually creates a new CCDS version?
options: A labelling committee decision, for example after a safety signal
questions.why: The CCDS changes when the company's position changes, typically after a signal, new data or an agency request.

questions.q: Why is a CCDS version frozen once it is effective?
options: So every label can be traced to the exact text it was assessed against
Because it is printed on the carton
So it can be submitted as SPL
questions.why: Labels are mapped to a specific version; changing an effective version would break that trace. Changes go into a new version.

questions.q: Who approves the CCDS?
options: The company (for example its labelling committee)
questions.why: The CCDS is the company's own document. Agencies approve local labels.

questions.q: A CCSI statement is missing from the US label and no reason is recorded. What is it?
options: Only a problem if FDA asks
An unjustified deviation that must be fixed or justified
questions.why: Every deviation from the CCSI needs a documented justification.

questions.q: Which is an acceptable deviation justification?
options: FDA did not accept the proposed wording in the 2025 review (letter on file)
questions.why: A justification names a real reason that can be checked: an agency decision, a local requirement, an indication not approved.

questions.q: Does mapping require the label to repeat the CCDS word for word?
options: No, it must say the same thing in substance
questions.why: Local labels follow local format and style; alignment is about meaning.

questions.q: A CCDS dosing statement covers an indication not approved in the US. How is it recorded?
questions.why: "Not applicable" still needs a reason, here that the indication is not approved in the market.

questions.q: Where might one CCDS warning appear in a US PLR label?
options: Highlights, section 5, section 17 and the Medication Guide
questions.why: A warning is summarised in Highlights, described in 5.x, used in counselling (17) and explained to patients in the Medication Guide.

questions.q: In this app, what happens if a CCSI statement is neither found nor justified?
options: A warning that can be waived
questions.why: The CORE-MAP rule treats an unexplained CCSI gap as an error.

questions.q: After a 505(o)(4) notification, how long does the holder have to respond?
questions.why: The holder must submit a supplement or a rebuttal within 30 days.

questions.q: What are the two ways to respond to a 505(o)(4) notification?
options: A phone call or an email
A new NDA or an ANDA
A supplement with proposed changes, or a rebuttal giving reasons no change is warranted
questions.why: The statute allows a labelling supplement or a statement that the holder believes no change is warranted, with reasons.

questions.q: If FDA disagrees with the response, how long can discussions last?
questions.why: Discussions are limited to 30 days, after which FDA may order the change within 15 days.

questions.q: Which route lets a holder strengthen a warning before FDA approves it?
questions.why: Changes that add or strengthen a warning can be made on submission of a Changes Being Effected supplement.

questions.q: An agency comment asks you to delete "superior efficacy" from section 14. Best response?
options: Accept and delete it, unless you have adequate head-to-head data in the application
Move it to the Medication Guide
questions.why: Comparative claims need substantial evidence; labelling must not be promotional or misleading.

questions.q: What belongs in a response table for agency comments?
options: The reviewer's name and phone number
Each comment, the decision, the reason and where the text changed
questions.why: A full response table lets the reviewer check every comment quickly.

questions.q: When is a labelling change "implemented"?
options: When the agency receives the submission
When packs with the new labelling are being distributed
questions.why: Implementation means the new labelling is in use on product leaving the company.

questions.q: Where does final US labelling go in the eCTD?
questions.why: Module 1.14 holds labelling: 1.14.1 draft, 1.14.2 final, 1.14.3 listed drug labelling.

questions.q: Why track a CCDS change per market?
options: Each market has its own submission, classification, review time and implementation date
Because the CCDS is different in each market
Only to report to the WHO
questions.why: One core change becomes many local changes, each on its own clock.

questions.q: In this app, the 90-day target to first shipment is…
options: A training default the company would set in its procedures
questions.why: There is no single legal deadline; companies set their own targets. The app labels its defaults as such.

questions.q: Which file does this app hand to pharmacovigilance?
options: The current CCSI as reference safety information
questions.why: PV uses the CCSI to decide whether reactions are listed.

questions.q: What does "old stock out" record?
options: The date the CCDS was drafted
The date by which packs with the old labelling have left the company's control
The expiry date of the product
questions.why: It closes the implementation: after it, only the new labelling is distributed.

questions.q: Which CIOMS working group introduced core safety information?
questions.why: CIOMS III set out the idea of core safety information; CIOMS V developed it.
questions.cite: CIOMS Working Groups III and V

questions.q: Which ICH guideline uses the CCSI as reference safety information in periodic reports?
questions.why: The PBRER compares reactions against the reference safety information, usually the CCSI.

questions.q: The EU SmPC does not carry a CCDS statement because the EU agreed other wording. How is it mapped?
options: The SmPC is changed to copy the CCDS
As a deviation with a justification
questions.why: Local labels may differ for regulatory reasons; the deviation is recorded and justified.

questions.q: In this app, where must a statement's key terms appear for it to count as found?
options: In the sections the statement is mapped to
questions.why: Each statement names its target sections for each kind of label.

questions.q: What does a PRAC signal recommendation set?
options: The product information wording and a deadline to submit
questions.why: PRAC recommendations give wording in all EU languages and a deadline for the variation.

questions.q: Which trigger in this app has a response clock set by statute?
questions.why: 505(o)(4) gives 30 days to respond; company targets are internal choices.

questions.q: Where does EU product information go in the eCTD?
questions.why: 1.3.1 holds the SmPC, Annex II, labelling and package leaflet.

questions.q: In US Module 1, what goes in 1.14.1?
questions.why: 1.14.1 is draft labeling, 1.14.2 final labeling, 1.14.3 listed drug labeling.
